name: Scale-Split Nonlocal F+ with Independent Stiff Vector (SSNF+ISV)
claimed_mechanism: Uses two distinct spatial operators to satisfy the scale-split theorem: a heavy local mass gaps the 's' mode (freeze), while a light nonlocal operator (-D^2)^-1 builds the F+ kernel (fidelity). The stiff vector u_mu supplies the necessary preferred-frame carrier for lensing slip (DC-013), but its kinetic normalization is independent of the screened coupling e^-y, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wound.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the nonlocal F+ term generates the MOND force law. The screened preferred-frame coupling e^-y ensures alpha_1 and alpha_2 vanish in the high-acceleration Solar System limit. The stiff vector provides the off-ray metric slip (Psi != Phi) required for correct MOND lensing, while its independent kinetic term prevents the divergence of the longitudinal mode normalization.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is structurally distinct from DC-014 (stiff vector kill) because the vector's kinetic normalization is explicitly independent of the screened coupling, breaking the P7 identification. It is distinct from DC-011 (single-mass localization) by using a scale-split two-operator structure. It is distinct from DC-013 (frame-free slip-lock) by including a preferred-frame carrier. It is distinct from DC-010 (khronometric) by using a spatially nonlocal realization instead of a khronon field.
